paper.abstract_en: QEpy is a Python electronic-structure software package based on Quantum ESPRESSO (QE). QEpy accomplishes two goals. First, it simplifies running and prototyping calculations with QE. Second, it targets nonstandard workflows where the electronic-structure engine is used in ways for which it was not originally designed. For example, QEpy can instruct QE to run with custom potentials in the Hamiltonian, including external, exchange-correlation, and local pseudopotentials. QEpy also exposes, at any point during an electronic-structure calculation, including between self-consistent-field cycles, quantities that would normally be accessible only through post-processing, such as the electron density and wavefunctions. QEpy’s API to the Atomic Simulation Environment gives direct access to ASE-based workflows and tools. These capabilities make QEpy a flexible platform for implementing custom workflows, interfacing QE with other simulation tools, and prototyping new electronic-structure methods. This work is written in a hybrid paper/tutorial style. Several example notebooks are presented, together with references to publications in which QEpy has already been employed. Our goal is for QEpy to serve as a versatile platform for research, teaching, and innovation in electronic-structure theory and method development.
